newsitem.title: USA: OshKosh B'Gosh sees Q1 earnings hurt.
newsitem.headline: OshKosh B'Gosh sees Q1 earnings hurt.

text.p: OshKosh B'Gosh Inc said on Wednesday a strategic decision to decrease distribution over the next two years would reduce first quarter earnings.

"As a result of this decision, along with other business and competitive factors, we will be facing an anticipated 25 percent reduction in our wholesale business in the first quarter of 1997 as compared to 1996, resulting in significantly lower first quarter 1997 earnings," said chief executive Douglas Hyde said in a news release.
The company reported net income of $3.3 million, or $0.27 a share, in the 1996 first quarter.

The children's apparel maker also said it currently anticipates an increase in its net royalty income from foreign licensees of more than 40 percent, after winding down its European business operations and moving this business to a licensee.
Anticipated growth in other foreign markets will also lead to higher net royalty income, the company said.
Earlier Wednesday, the company reported a net loss of $0.22, or $2.6 million a share, after special charges, compared to net profit of $1.7 million, or $0.14 a share a year ago.
OshKosh shares closed up 1/8 at 14-7/8 Wednesday.
